questions.question: India celebrated the 146th birth anniversary of which of the following famous social reformers and rationalists from Tamil Nadu on 17 September 2024?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Periyar EV Ramasamy**, popularly known as **Periyar**, was a prominent **social reformer** and **rationalist** from Tamil Nadu.
 
• He was born on **17 September 1879** in **Erode**, Tamil Nadu, and is regarded as the **Father of the Dravidian Movement**.
 
• Periyar was a strong advocate of **social justice, equality, and self-respect**, particularly focusing on the rights and empowerment of the **marginalized communities**.
 
• He founded the **Self-Respect Movement** in 1925, aimed at eradicating caste discrimination, promoting gender equality, and opposing religious orthodoxy.
 
• Periyar was vocal against the dominance of **Brahminical ideologies** and Hindu rituals, which he believed perpetuated inequality.
 
• He played a critical role in advocating for **rationalism** and the importance of scientific temper in society.
 
• Periyar’s ideas and movements significantly influenced the political landscape of Tamil Nadu, including the rise of the **Dravidian political parties** such as the **DMK** and **AIADMK**.
 
• His contributions to social reform earned him the title of **"Vaikom Hero"** for his participation in the Vaikom Satyagraha, which fought against untouchability.
 
• Periyar’s legacy continues to be celebrated for his efforts to build an egalitarian society, and his birth anniversary is widely observed to honor his contributions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **MK Stalin**__

 __
 
• **MK Stalin** is the current **Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu** and the son of former CM **Karunanidhi**.
 
• He is a prominent political leader in Tamil Nadu, representing the **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)** party.
 
• MK Stalin has focused on social welfare schemes, education reform, and economic development in Tamil Nadu during his tenure.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**__
 __
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as the **Father of the Nation** in India, was a leading figure in the Indian **freedom struggle**.
 
• He championed the principles of **non-violence (Ahimsa)** and **Satyagraha** as methods to resist colonial oppression.
 
• Gandhi’s efforts in movements like the **Salt March** and **Quit India Movement** were pivotal in India gaining independence from British rule.
 
 
 
• **Radhakrishnan**__
 
 
• **Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan** was the **second President of India** and a renowned philosopher and scholar.
 
• His birthday, **5th September**, is celebrated as **Teachers’ Day** in India, honoring his contributions to education.
 
• Radhakrishnan was an advocate for **interfaith dialogue** and a proponent of Indian philosophy on the global stage.

questions.question: Which event led to the formation of the Muslim League in 1906?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Partition of Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary event that led to the formation of the Muslim League in 1906 was the **Partition of Bengal in 1905.**
 
• This partition, which created a Muslim-majority East Bengal, heightened communal tensions and prompted Muslim leaders to seek a political platform to protect their interests and ensure their representation in British India.
 
• The Muslim League emerged as a political organization aimed at protecting the interests of Muslims in India and played a significant role in shaping the political discourse leading to India's partition.
 
• This event also marked the beginning of communal politics in India, with separate electorates becoming a contentious issue in the subsequent decades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Partition of Bengal**__

 __
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** was announced in **1905** by Lord Curzon. It divided Bengal into two provinces: **East Bengal** and **West Bengal**.
 
• The decision was justified on administrative grounds but was perceived by Indians as a strategy to divide and weaken the **nationalist movement**.
 
• It led to widespread protests and the launch of the **Swadeshi Movement**, which aimed to promote indigenous industries and boycott British goods.
 
• The partition was revoked in **1911** due to intense opposition and protests from Indians.
 
 
 
• **Simla Deputation**__
 __
 
• The Simla Deputation was a pivotal event in Indian history, held in October 1906, where a group of prominent Muslim leaders led by Aga Khan met the then Viceroy, Lord Minto, in Simla.
 
• The deputation aimed to present the concerns of the Muslim community and request special representation for Muslims in the legislative councils to safeguard their political rights.
 
• The leaders expressed their apprehensions about being politically and socially marginalized within the larger framework of Indian society, especially under a system of representative governance dominated by the majority community.
 
• They requested separate electorates for Muslims, enabling them to elect their own representatives.
 
• The Viceroy, Lord Minto, assured the delegation of his support for the demands, marking a significant step toward the institutional recognition of communal representation in India.
 
 
 
• **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**__
 __
 
• The **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**, also known as the **Government of India Act 1919**, introduced the concept of **diarchy** in provincial governments.
 
• It aimed to provide limited self-governance by dividing subjects into **reserved** and **transferred lists**.
 
• The reforms were criticized for their limited scope and lack of full autonomy, eventually leading to the rise of **nationalist movements**.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act**__
 
 
• The **Indian Councils Act** was introduced in **1892** to expand legislative councils and increase Indian representation in governance.
 
• It allowed members of the councils to discuss budgets and address questions to the administration, but it provided limited power to Indian representatives.
 
• The act was a precursor to subsequent reforms aimed at increasing Indian participation in governance.

questions.question: Dubnium, an artificially produced radioactive transuranium element with atomic number 105, is present in which group of the periodic table?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Group 5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dubnium** is an artificially produced radioactive **transuranium element** with an atomic number of **105**.
 
• It is classified as a member of **Group 5** in the periodic table.
 
• Group 5 elements are characterized by their **valence electron configuration**, which is typically **d¹s²**, meaning they have one electron in their **d-orbital**.
 
• Other elements in Group 5 include **vanadium (V)**, **niobium (Nb)**, and **tantalum (Ta)**, which share similar chemical properties.
 
• **Dubnium** is named after the Russian town of **Dubna**, where it was first synthesized at the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research.
 
• Like other transuranium elements, **Dubnium** is highly unstable and exists only in minute quantities in laboratory settings.
 
• Its most stable isotope is **Dubnium-268**, which has a half-life of approximately **16 hours**.
 
• Elements in Group 5 exhibit **high melting points**, **metallic bonding**, and strong **oxidizing properties**.
 
• They are often used in studies involving **nuclear chemistry** and high-energy physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Group 3**__

 __
 
• Group 3 includes elements like **scandium (Sc)**, **yttrium (Y)**, and the **lanthanides**.
 
• These elements are known for their **rare earth properties** and are widely used in **electronics** and **magnets**.
 
• They exhibit a valence electron configuration of **d¹s²**, similar to Group 5, but their chemical behavior differs significantly.
 
 
 
• **Group 7**__
 __
 
• Group 7 elements include **manganese (Mn)**, **technetium (Tc)**, and **rhenium (Re)**.
 
• These elements are characterized by their **multiple oxidation states** and are used in **catalysts**, **medical imaging**, and **alloys**.
 
• Technetium, like Dubnium, is radioactive but belongs to a different group due to its distinct **electron configuration**.
 
 
 
• **Group 11**__
 
 
• Group 11 includes **copper (Cu)**, **silver (Ag)**, and **gold (Au)**.
 
• These elements are known as **coinage metals** due to their historical use in currency.
 
• They are highly **conductive** and possess unique **electrical and thermal properties**.

questions.question: Which of the following neighbouring countries of India has the lowest population density?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bhutan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhutan** has the **lowest population density** among the neighbouring countries of India.
 
• The population density of Bhutan is approximately **20 people per square kilometre**, which is very low compared to other neighbouring nations.
 
• Bhutan is a **landlocked country** located in the eastern Himalayas, bordered by **India** to the south and **China** to the north.
 
• The country's small population is distributed over a large area of rugged terrain, contributing to its low density.
 
• The landscape of Bhutan is dominated by **mountains and forests**, which further restricts urbanization and dense settlements.
 
• Bhutan follows a policy of **Gross National Happiness (GNH)**, emphasizing sustainable development and environmental conservation.
 
• Major cities like **Thimphu** (the capital) and **Paro** are sparsely populated compared to urban centres in other countries.
 
• Bhutan's focus on preserving its **cultural heritage** and environment limits population growth and infrastructure expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nepal**__

 __
 
• **Nepal** has a population density of around **200 people per square kilometre**, significantly higher than Bhutan.
 
• Nepal is located in the **Himalayan region** and is bordered by India and China.
 
• The country's population is concentrated in the **Terai region**, which is fertile and suitable for agriculture.
 
• Nepal is known for its famous mountain ranges, including **Mount Everest**, the world's highest peak.
 
 
 
• **Bangladesh**__
 __
 
• **Bangladesh** has one of the highest population densities in the world, with over **1200 people per square kilometre**.
 
• It is a densely populated country located in the eastern region of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The fertile plains of the **Ganges-Brahmaputra delta** support a large population.
 
• Major cities like **Dhaka** (the capital) and **Chittagong** are heavily urbanized and densely populated.
 
 
 
• **Pakistan**__
 
 
• **Pakistan** has a population density of approximately **287 people per square kilometre**.
 
• The population is concentrated in regions like **Punjab** and **Sindh**, which are agriculturally rich.
 
• Major cities like **Karachi**, **Lahore**, and **Islamabad** have significant urban populations.
 
• Pakistan's diverse geography includes **mountains**, **deserts**, and fertile plains, influencing population distribution.

questions.question: KD Jadhav has won the Olympics medal in which of the following sports?

• Jadhav won the **bronze medal** in the **Bantamweight category** of freestyle wrestling.
 
• His achievement was especially significant as it came at a time when India was newly independent, showcasing the country's potential in international sports.
 
• He trained under **Rees Gardner**, a coach from the United States, and received significant support from his family and local community.
 
• Jadhav was known for his **agility, strength, and determination**, which helped him compete against some of the best wrestlers in the world.
 
• After his Olympic success, KD Jadhav became a symbol of **Indian pride** and inspired many young athletes in India to pursue wrestling.
 
• In recognition of his contribution to sports, a **stadium** named after him, the **Shri Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Complex KD Jadhav Stadium**, was established in Pune.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• Weightlifting is a sport where athletes lift heavy weights in specific techniques such as **snatch** and **clean and jerk**.
 
• India has seen success in weightlifting in recent years, with athletes like **Mirabai Chanu** winning medals at the Olympics.
 
• However, KD Jadhav did not win his Olympic medal in weightlifting.
 
 
 
• **Boxing**__
 __
 
• Boxing is a combat sport where two participants compete using their fists while wearing gloves.
 
• India has produced successful boxers like **Mary Kom** and **Vijender Singh**, who have won medals in international competitions.
 
• Although boxing is a popular sport in India, KD Jadhav’s Olympic medal was not won in boxing.
 
 
 
• **Shooting**__
 
 
• Shooting is a precision sport where competitors aim at targets using firearms.
 
• India has excelled in shooting with athletes like **Abhinav Bindra**, who won a **gold medal** at the **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• Despite India’s success in shooting, KD Jadhav’s achievement was in wrestling, not shooting.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution encourages the protection and improvement of the environment, as well as the safeguarding of forests and wildlife?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 48A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 48A** of the Indian Constitution is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which guides the state in formulating policies for the welfare of its citizens.
 
• This article explicitly emphasizes the need for the **protection and improvement of the environment** and the safeguarding of **forests and wildlife**.
 
• It was introduced by the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**, which expanded the scope of environmental protection in India.
 
• The article directs the state to take proactive measures to preserve and improve the environment, ensuring a balance between development and ecological sustainability.
 
• Article 48A complements **Article 51A(g)**, which imposes a duty on citizens to protect the environment and have compassion for living creatures.
 
• This provision is vital in the context of India’s growing industrialization and urbanization, which have led to significant **environmental challenges**, including deforestation, pollution, and loss of biodiversity.
 
• Article 48A has inspired numerous laws and regulations in India, such as the **Wildlife Protection Act**, **Forest Conservation Act**, and **Environment Protection Act**, aimed at safeguarding natural resources.

questions.question: Who among the following nominates one-sixth members to the state legislative council of a state in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor** is the constitutional head of a state in India and acts on the advice of the **Council of Ministers**.
 
• Under **Article 171** of the Indian Constitution, the State Legislative Council consists of members who are elected and nominated.
 
• The Governor has the power to **nominate one-sixth of the members** of the State Legislative Council.
 
• The nominated members are chosen from fields like **literature, science, art, cooperative movement, and social service.**
 
• This provision ensures representation of **eminent personalities** who might not be elected through regular electoral procedures.
 
• The nomination process helps in maintaining a balance between **technical expertise** and **political representation** within the legislative council.
 
• The Governor's role in this context emphasizes the importance of a **non-partisan and inclusive approach** to governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** State Election Commissioner**__

 __
 
• The **State Election Commissioner** is responsible for conducting elections for local bodies such as **panchayats** and **municipalities** within the state.
 
• This position is independent of the legislative council nomination process.
 
• The State Election Commissioner operates under the **supervision of the Election Commission of India** and is governed by provisions of the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments**.
 
 
 
• ** President**__
 __
 
• The **President** of India is the constitutional head of the union government and has powers related to the **Parliament**, not the State Legislative Council.
 
• While the President nominates members to the **Rajya Sabha**, they do not have a role in nominating members to a state’s legislative council.
 
 
 
• ** Chief Minister**__
 
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the government in a state and leads the **executive branch**.
 
• Although the Chief Minister advises the Governor, they do not have the power to nominate members to the State Legislative Council directly.
 
• The Chief Minister’s role is primarily focused on **administrative and policy-making decisions** within the state.

questions.question: Which industry focuses on transforming raw materials into finished products?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Manufacturing industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Manufacturing industry** focuses on transforming **raw materials** into **finished products** through various processes such as **assembly, design, fabrication, and production.**
 
• It is a part of the **secondary sector** of the economy, which deals with the processing of raw goods obtained from the **primary sector**.
 
• The industry encompasses a wide range of activities, including **automobile production, electronics, textiles, food processing, and machinery manufacturing.**
 
• Manufacturing industries play a crucial role in the economic development of a country by contributing to **GDP, employment generation, and export earnings.**
 
• Examples of manufacturing industries include companies like **Tata Motors, Samsung, and Nestle** that produce cars, electronics, and processed food products, respectively.
 
• These industries depend on advancements in **technology, innovation, skilled labor, and infrastructure** to increase efficiency and quality.
 
• Manufacturing industries often contribute to the global supply chain by distributing goods internationally.
 
• They also promote the development of **industrial areas** and encourage investments in **research and development** to improve production techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Genetic industry**__

 __
 
• The **Genetic industry** involves activities related to the **cultivation and breeding of plants and animals** to improve their genetic characteristics.
 
• Examples include **agriculture, aquaculture, and animal husbandry.**
 
• This industry focuses on producing raw materials, such as **crops, livestock, and fish**, rather than finished goods.
 
 
 
• **Service industry**__
 __
 
• The **Service industry** provides **intangible services** such as **education, healthcare, tourism, and financial services** rather than physical products.
 
• It is part of the **tertiary sector** of the economy and focuses on meeting the needs of consumers and businesses.
 
• Examples include **banks, hospitals, schools, and IT service companies.**
 
 
 
• **Primary industry**__
 
 
• The **Primary industry** focuses on the extraction and harvesting of **natural resources**, such as **mining, agriculture, forestry, and fishing.**
 
• This sector provides the raw materials used by the **manufacturing industry** for producing finished goods.
 
• Examples include **coal mining, wheat farming, and timber harvesting.**

questions.question: Which chemical found in the peels of citrus fruits is used as a flavouring agent in beverages and chewing gums?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Limonene**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Limonene** is a naturally occurring chemical compound primarily found in the **peels of citrus fruits**, such as oranges, lemons, and limes.
 
• It is a type of **terpene**, which is a large and diverse class of organic compounds produced by various plants.
 
• **Limonene** is widely used as a **flavoring agent** in beverages and chewing gums due to its characteristic **citrus aroma and taste**.
 
• In addition to its use in food products, limonene is also employed in **aromatherapy** and as a natural solvent in cleaning products.
 
• The compound is known for its **antioxidant** and anti-inflammatory properties, making it a subject of interest in medical research.
 
• It is extracted from citrus peel oil using a process called **steam distillation**.
 
• In the food and beverage industry, limonene is classified as **GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe)** by the **US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Lutidine**__

 __
 
• **Lutidine** refers to a group of organic compounds that are isomers of **dimethylpyridine**.
 
• It is primarily used in the **pharmaceutical** and **chemical industries** as a solvent or intermediate in the synthesis of other chemicals.
 
• Lutidines do not have flavoring properties and are not used in food or beverage products.
 
 
 
• **Menthone**__
 __
 
• **Menthone** is a naturally occurring organic compound found in **mint oils**.
 
• It is commonly used as a **fragrance** in perfumes and as a flavoring agent in some products, but it is not the primary flavoring agent in citrus-based beverages or chewing gums.
 
• It has a characteristic **minty aroma** and is a key component of peppermint oil.
 
 
 
• **Ethylvanillin**__
 
 
• **Ethylvanillin** is a synthetic compound that is used as a **vanilla flavoring agent**.
 
• It is stronger and more concentrated than natural vanilla, making it a popular choice in **confectionery, baked goods, and ice creams**.
 
• Unlike limonene, ethylvanillin is not derived from natural sources but is synthesized chemically.

questions.question: Water cycle is the process by which water is circulated in the environment in different forms among:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**oceans, atmosphere, and land**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **water cycle**, also known as the **hydrological cycle**, is a natural process through which water is continuously circulated in various forms across the **oceans, atmosphere, and land**.
 
• It involves processes such as **evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, and runoff**, ensuring the movement of water through different reservoirs.
 
• Water evaporates from the surface of **oceans, rivers, lakes, and other water bodies** due to the heat provided by the **sun**.
 
• In the atmosphere, water vapor cools and condenses to form **clouds**, which eventually result in precipitation such as **rain, snow, or hail**.
 
• On land, precipitation contributes to processes like **infiltration** (where water seeps into the soil) and **surface runoff** (where water flows over the surface into rivers and streams).
 
• A significant portion of the water eventually returns to the **oceans**, completing the cycle.
 
• This cycle is essential for maintaining the **Earth's water balance** and supporting life by replenishing **freshwater resources**.
 
• The water cycle also plays a critical role in regulating the **Earth's climate** and weather patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Clouds and atmosphere**__

 __
 
• The **clouds** and the **atmosphere** represent key components of the water cycle, specifically in the processes of **condensation and precipitation**.
 
• However, these are not the only components of the water cycle, as it also involves reservoirs like **oceans, rivers, and land areas**.
 
 
 
• **Rivers and oceans**__
 __
 
• While **rivers** and **oceans** are important reservoirs for water, they do not represent the entire water cycle.
 
• The water cycle also involves the **atmosphere** and land processes like **evaporation, infiltration, and runoff**.
 
 
 
• **Land and ocean**__
 
 
• **Land** and **oceans** are essential reservoirs for the water cycle, but this option excludes the role of the **atmosphere**, where critical processes like **evaporation** and **condensation** occur.

questions.question: Indian classical vocalist Rashid Khan belonged to which of the following gharanas of music?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Rampur - Sahaswan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rampur - Sahaswan** gharana is one of the prominent **gharanas of Hindustani classical music**.
 
• It is known for its emphasis on **pure classical music** and its rich repertoire of compositions.
 
• This gharana originated in the **Rampur and Sahaswan regions**, primarily under the patronage of the rulers of Rampur.
 
• The Rampur - Sahaswan gharana is closely associated with the legacy of **Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan**, who was instrumental in its development.
 
• Artists belonging to this gharana are renowned for their **melodious and intricate renditions** of ragas.
 
• Its vocal style is characterized by the use of **slow-tempo elaborations** and distinctive taans (rapid melodic passages).
 
• **Rashid Khan**, a celebrated Indian classical vocalist, belongs to this gharana and has been recognized for his mastery and innovation in Hindustani classical music.
 
• Rashid Khan is regarded as a **torchbearer** of the Rampur - Sahaswan gharana, blending traditional techniques with his own creative expressions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gwalior Gharana**__

 __
 
• **Gwalior gharana** is considered the oldest and most influential gharana of Hindustani classical music.
 
• It originated in the **Gwalior region** of Madhya Pradesh and gained prominence during the reign of Raja Man Singh Tomar.
 
• Gwalior gharana is known for its emphasis on **dhrupad and khayal singing styles**.
 
• Its compositions are characterized by **clarity and structure**, with a focus on detailed elaboration of ragas.
 
 
 
• **Atrauli - Jaipur Gharana**__
 __
 
• The **Atrauli - Jaipur gharana** is known for its intricate and highly sophisticated vocal techniques.
 
• It originated in the **Jaipur region** and was developed by **Alladiya Khan**.
 
• Artists from this gharana are recognized for their mastery of **rare and complex ragas**.
 
• It emphasizes the use of **layakari (rhythmic play)** and meend (gliding notes).
 
 
 
• **Lucknow Gharana**__
 
 
• The **Lucknow gharana** is primarily known for its contributions to **Thumri and Kathak dance**.
 
• It originated in the **Lucknow region** under the patronage of Nawabs of Awadh.
 
• Lucknow gharana focuses on **expressive and emotive singing styles**, often blending classical and semi-classical elements.
 
• It is characterized by the use of **delicate ornamentation** in compositions.

questions.question: In March 2024, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, a 1988 batch Uttarakhand cadre officer of the Indian Administrative Service, joined which of the following departments of the Indian Government?

options.text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Election Commission of India (ECI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sukhbir Singh Sandhu**, a 1988 batch officer of the **Indian Administrative Service** (IAS) and belonging to the **Uttarakhand cadre**, joined the **Election Commission of India (ECI)** in March 2024.
 
• The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is an independent constitutional authority responsible for administering elections in India at the **national, state, and local levels**.
 
• It operates under the provisions of **Article 324** of the **Indian Constitution**, ensuring free and fair elections.
 
• The Commission is composed of a **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)** and two other **Election Commissioners**.
 
• **Sukhbir Singh Sandhu** is known for his vast administrative experience and was previously involved in crucial roles, such as serving as the **Chairman of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**.
 
• His appointment to the ECI reflects the importance of experienced administrators in maintaining the integrity of India’s electoral processes.
 
• The ECI is tasked with ensuring compliance with the **Model Code of Conduct**, managing voter registration, and supervising the election process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**__

 __
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the **central bank of India**, established in **1935**.
 
• Its primary functions include regulating the **monetary policy**, maintaining financial stability, and issuing currency.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in managing **inflation**, supervising banks, and ensuring economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**__
 __
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** is a constitutional body established under **Article 315** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It conducts examinations for appointments to the **All India Services** and other key government posts.
 
• UPSC is responsible for recruiting personnel based on merit and ensures a transparent selection process.
 
 
 
• **Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)**__
 
 
• The **Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)** is an independent authority established under **Article 148** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The CAG audits the accounts of the Union, State Governments, and public sector organizations.
 
• It ensures accountability in the usage of public funds and submits audit reports to the **President of India**.
